authority: OW-6: the Fable boss decides when risk, dependencies and blast radius require a human, and presents the choices with its recommendation and the alternatives' pros and cons. The orchestrator surfaces the packet and does NOT decide the escalated question.

A_track_rule.ruled: HARD if and only if at least THREE of the five criteria score 3 (the rubric's 'severe, a principal driver of difficulty for this book'). Equivalent in totals: every book with total >= 13 is HARD (13 cannot be reached with fewer than three 3s: 3+3+2+2+2 = 12), and a book at 12 is HARD only when its 12 is composed of three 3s (Acts). A single criterion at 3 does NOT force HARD; it forces that book's extra_scrutiny_focus regions to be carried as FLAGGED REGIONS in its brief (Fable-boss escalation target, final-checker attention, and my recommendation that the no-sampling-shortcut arm apply to those regions even on the STANDARD track). Applied without exception after the two named adjustments.
alternatives_offered: A1: any criterion at 3 forces HARD (30 HARD / 12 STANDARD on the adjusted scores)
A2: total >= 13 (14 HARD: the ruled set minus Acts)
A3: total >= 12 (19 HARD: the ruled set plus Joel, Matt, Mark, Jude; 2Cor would join only at its pre-adjustment 12)
A4: total >= 14 (8 HARD: Ezek, Dan, Rev, Hos, Mic, Hab, Zech, Rom)

B_greek_substrate.finding: no Greek New Testament source text is staged for this campaign; four scorers reported it independently
B_greek_substrate.ruling: a staged Greek substrate is a Phase-0 precondition for every NT book on either track; WHICH witness is an owner decision
B_greek_substrate.recommendation: Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine Textform primary (public domain, verse existence matches the translation one-to-one) plus SBLGNT secondary (CC BY 4.0) for critical-text divergence disclosure
alternatives_offered: B1 (recommended): Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine Textform primary + SBLGNT secondary
B4: a public-domain critical text (Nestle 1904 or Westcott-Hort 1881)
B5: no Greek substrate; run the NT on WEB alone
B6: build the substrate but shake it down out of canonical order on 3John, 2John or Phlm before Matt
B_greek_substrate.licence_caveat: licence and edition facts are stated from the agent's memory and MUST be verified at staging; nothing in the packet is a confirmed staging fact

does_not_block: Lamentations continues to its close; the escalation binds the books after it. The lane must not cross from Malachi to Matthew without a decision on B.
reversibility: upward re-classification stays open at every Phase 0; a book run STANDARD that should have been HARD cannot recover controlling-agent authorship of its boundaries after they are drawn
